intended_object: The forgetful conversion that takes a split Artin–Wedderburn presentation A ≃ₐ[K] ∏ᵢ M_{nᵢ}(K) and views it as a general algebraic Wedderburn presentation in which every coefficient division algebra is K itself. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition does exactly what its docstring says. It keeps the block count, the degrees and the algebra equivalence, and sets every coefficient division ring to `fun _ ↦ K`.

The structure fields are filled from the ambient instances: the division ring structure from `Field K`, the K-algebra structure from `Algebra.id`, and positivity of the degrees from `P.instNeZeroDegree`. With these choices the type of `P.equiv`, `A ≃ₐ[K] ∀ i, Matrix (Fin (degree i)) (Fin (degree i)) K`, matches the type the target structure expects, so the equivalence carries over unchanged.

The universe choice `{u, v, v}` is forced by putting `K : Type v` in as the coefficient type. The generality is right: a split presentation is only defined over a field K (`SplitWedderburnAlgebraPresentation` takes `[Field K]`), and that is the only setting this conversion uses.

Mathlib has no such presentation structures, so there is no counterpart. The map is a library-specific forgetful map, but it is mathematically meaningful (every split presentation is in particular a presentation) and it is implemented correctly.
